items.quote: Protocols like MESI (Modified, Exclusive, Shared, Invalid) act as a "law of the land" inside the chip
A cancerous state, for instance, can be seen as a form of protocol violation, where a single cell ignores system-wide signals

items.target: a far more fundamental protocol embedded in the fabric of physics itself
items.quote: This engineered protocol in silicon serves as a powerful metaphor for a far more fundamental protocol embedded in the fabric of physics itself.
This coherent superposition is the ultimate state of internal consistency, holding multiple potentials in a delicate harmony.
It is destroyed through any unwanted interaction with the surrounding environment, a process known as decoherence.
In Quantum Resource Theories (QRT), quantum coherence is treated not as an abstract property but as a tangible, finite commodity.
Decoherence acts as the universe's most fundamental protocol.

the pattern is an *emergent property* of these local interactions

items.target: Once this higher-level structure forms, it begins to constrain the behavior of the very agents that created it
items.quote: Once this higher-level structure forms, it begins to constrain the behavior of the very agents that created it, a phenomenon known as **downward causation**
It can be an emergent property that arises from the bottom up, where a system generates its own internal rules
Cache Coherence Protocols (e.g., MESI) enforce a shared, single truth through a "social contract" between cores.
Decoherence forces superposition to collapse, acting as a universal "correspondence check" against the environment.
Self-Organization generates emergent global order through local rules and the sacrifice of individual freedom.
The Coherence Kernel (K₁): The domain of reversible computation, information preservation, and self-sustaining order.
The Collapse Kernel (K₀): The domain of irreversible computation, entropy, and information erasure.
